UPSTREAM: Input: document meanings of KEY_SCREEN and KEY_ZOOM It is hard to say what KEY_SCREEN and KEY_ZOOM mean, but historically DVB folks have used them to indicate switch to full screen mode. Later, they converged on using KEY_ZOOM to switch into full screen mode and KEY)SCREEN to control aspect ratio (see Documentation/media/uapi/rc/rc-tables.rst). Let's commit to these uses, and define: - KEY_FULL_SCREEN (and make KEY_ZOOM its alias) - KEY_ASPECT_RATIO (and make KEY_SCREEN its alias) Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com> BUG=b:135045276 TEST=Build (cherry picked from commit 07ba9e7be423423043c5090a2f395c0da26e1b3d) Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Change-Id: I8863dd12d794c1cd3ea52fe131975d735a45750c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromiumos/third_party/kernel/+/1689755 Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@google.com> (cherry picked from commit d281074b6ccca0a6f8477a784c28a12a3503363e) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1690114 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: adapter: Prevent cleaning up temporary devices during active scanning. bluetoothd is supposed to clean up temporary devices after 3 minutes of scanning absence, the logic was implemented using a timer that would be triggered 3 minutes after the last scanning stops. This could cause the following problem: 1. Chrome starts scanning. 2. Chrome stops scanning (timer starts counting to 3 minutes). 3. Nothing happens for 2 minutes 50 seconds. 4. Chrome starts scanning. 5. 10 seconds later, the timer created by step 2 triggers bluetoothd to clean up the scanning result (in the middle of Chrome scanning session). 6. Chrome stops scanning. In this change we cancel the timer if it exists when a new scanning starts. BUG=chromium:959306 TEST=manual tests via bluetoothctl with the following steps: 1. Turn scanning on 2. Turn scanning off after some devices have been discovered. 3. Count to 2 minutes 50 seconds. 4. Turn scanning on again. 5. Observe that the devices are not removed crossing the 3 minute mark. 6. Turn scanning off. 7. Wait for 3 minutes. 8. Observe the temp devices are deleted in the terminal. 9. The 'devices' command should return empty list. Change-Id: Ic84f8a8e77be308f210d8060e94a214524fb6f56 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1666588 Tested-by: Yu Liu <yudiliu@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Yu Liu <yudiliu@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth: Enable filter duplicates field for passive scan This sets the filter duplicates field in LE Set Scan Enabled command to enabled for passive scanning. By enabling the field, the advertisement reports from the same address would be sent to the host once per passive scan cycle. However, since the buffer to keep the seen address is limited (e.g. the size of buffer is 50 for Intel controllers), the host will still be interrupted by any advertisement report with new addresses beyond the size of the buffer. (2) Start btmon and confirm the mouse is connected by moving the mouse and observe ATT data in btmon. (3) Turn off the mouse and wait for 30 seconds. btmon prints HCI traffic of passive scanning. And the filtering duplicates was applied to at least 50 addresses in Bluetooth-noisy environment. Change-Id: I3a7b460facc6a1198c1a6f49cf476499f4ec91ca Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1682455 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

tast-test: arc.WindowManagerCUJ works on tablet devices arc.WindowmanagerCUJ is failing on certain tablet devices because the activity is being launched while the transition from tablet-to-clamshell mode is still in progress. At the moment we don't have a reliable way to "wait for transition to finish". So, this CL adds a timeout of 5 seconds (research in progress regarding how to get rid of the delay). This CL also cleans-up the code a bit, a make it more modular. Needed for a follow-up CL that will include more tests.
